elements_not_encoded.text: Manage urgently:
elements_not_encoded.reason: Section header for management steps; no criteria of its own.

elements_not_encoded.text: If patient just had a seizure 20.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Routes a patient who just had a seizure to page 20; seizure is already a recorded warning sign handled there.

elements_not_encoded.text: If aggressive/disruptive 35.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Routes aggressive/disruptive patients to page 35; Aggressive behavior is a recorded warning sign handled there.

elements_not_encoded.text: If recent head injury 30.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Routes recent head injury to page 30.

elements_not_encoded.text: If suicidal thoughts or plans 34.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Routes suicidal thoughts or plans to page 34.

elements_not_encoded.text: If difficulty breathing, respiratory rate > 30, oxygen saturation < 94% or oxygen saturation machine not available, give face mask oxygen.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Oxygen therapy criteria; management, no manage tasks in this pass.

elements_not_encoded.text: Check glucose: if < 3 (or < 4 if diabetes) or ≥ 11.1 19.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Glucose is a routine vital; the thresholds route to page 19 for management.

elements_not_encoded.text: If thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor, sunken eyes, decreased urine, give oral rehydration solution. If unable to drink or BP < 90/60, give sodium chloride 0.9
elements_not_encoded.reason: Rehydration and IV fluid management.

elements_not_encoded.text: Consider involuntary admission if signs of mental illness and refuses treatment/admission and a danger to self, others, own reputation or financial interest/pro
elements_not_encoded.reason: Involuntary admission decision (page 158); legal/management step.

elements_not_encoded.text: If HIV positive with recent positive cryptococcal antigen test, refer for urgent lumbar puncture (LP).
elements_not_encoded.reason: Referral for lumbar puncture; a lab result (CrAg) the language cannot express.

elements_not_encoded.text: Look for delirium, mania, psychosis, intoxication, withdrawal or poisoning and manage before referral:
elements_not_encoded.reason: Introduces the seven 'look for' boxes, each encoded as its own diagnosis rule.

elements_not_encoded.text: If no other sedation given, give diazepam 10mg orally.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Diazepam dose for withdrawal.

elements_not_encoded.text: Give thiamine 200mg IM.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Thiamine dose for alcohol intoxication.

elements_not_encoded.text: If pulse irregular, chest pain or BP ≥ 140/90, do ECG and discuss with specialist or local poison helpline 200.
elements_not_encoded.reason: ECG and specialist discussion in stimulant intoxication.

elements_not_encoded.text: If alcohol withdrawal, also give thiamine 200mg IM and oral rehydration solution.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Thiamine and ORS in alcohol withdrawal.

elements_not_encoded.text: Give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L 6 hourly.
elements_not_encoded.reason: IV fluids in alcohol intoxication.

elements_not_encoded.text: If ≥ 8 hours since last alcohol, refer for alcohol detoxification programme.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Referral for detoxification programme.

elements_not_encoded.text: Check for head injury.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Instruction to check for head injury in alcohol intoxication (assessment handled on page 30).

elements_not_encoded.text: Refer urgently unless:
elements_not_encoded.reason: Referral section header.

elements_not_encoded.text: Patient with known schizophrenia who is otherwise well, give routine schizophrenia care 162.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Referral exception (routine schizophrenia care, page 162).

elements_not_encoded.text: Patient with diabetes and low glucose on insulin. If abnormal thoughts/behaviour resolves with dextrose, no need to refer, give routine diabetes care 145.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Referral exception for hypoglycaemia resolving with dextrose (page 145).

elements_not_encoded.text: Patient with known alcohol use who is otherwise well. If abnormal thoughts/behaviour resolves once sober, no need to refer 165.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Referral exception for known alcohol use resolving once sober (page 165).
